geometry.note: OpenStreetMap alone yields at most 'approximate'; the link to the laboratory is not established, so the feature is context only.

method: OpenStreetMap way 1293533760 (man_made=mineshaft, name 'Shaft #8', area=yes, 44 m2) kept verbatim. Which mine shaft carries the laboratory's cages is not stated in the fetched sources; arXiv:0805.3170 Sec. 6.4.1 says only that equipment goes down 'a relatively small shaft dating to the days of iron mining' that 'is inclined by 12° with respect to the vertical'.
name: Soudan Mine 'Shaft #8' (OpenStreetMap)
notes: Informative: the laboratory shaft is inclined 12° from vertical and the detector midpoint is 705 m below the surface, so a straight shaft would put the level-27 station ~150 m horizontally from its collar (705 m x tan 12°); the detector midpoint is 127 m from the centroid of the NRHP shaft house and 72 m from this shaft collar. This is not a check: the detector is not at the shaft bottom and no source says which collar serves the laboratory.

summary.plain: A mine shaft collar at the Soudan Mine named 'Shaft #8' in OpenStreetMap, about 56 m north of the historic shaft house; which shaft serves the underground laboratory is not stated.
